verdicts.conflict: Whether open-source decentralized peer review can effectively manage and mitigate the dual-use safety risks of frontier AI models compared to closed corporate gatekeeping.
verdicts.rationale: Safetyists successfully undercut the accelerationist analogy by demonstrating that discovering software zero-day vulnerabilities differs fundamentally from proliferating autonomous frontier model capabilities. While accelerationists cite documented instances of open-source communities patching thousands of conventional software vulnerabilities, skeptics and safetyists highlight the absence of adequate compute infrastructure and legal protections in open-source ecosystems to safely audit frontier systems. Consequently, the safetyist position prevails on scope because it addresses the irreversible nature of capability diffusion rather than standard software debugging.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical demonstration that open-source communities can successfully isolate, audit, and contain autonomous frontier model weights without risking widespread diffusion of dangerous dual-use capabilities would tip the balance toward accelerationism.

verdicts.conflict: Whether open-source safety research sharing and compliance mandates primarily serve as mechanisms for corporate risk dumping and monopoly rent extraction rather than public protection.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics argue that compliance mandates externalize corporate risk and extract monopoly rents, but they offer limited empirical testing for alternative governance structures. Safetyists assert that boundary maintenance is necessary to prevent technological breakdown, yet they insufficiently account for the compliance burdens placed on municipal communities and independent researchers. Without concrete comparative data on compliance costs versus risk reduction across different lab sizes, the debate remains deadlocked on this normative point.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Comprehensive economic and safety audits measuring the actual distribution of liability costs and risk mitigation outcomes between dominant frontier labs and open-source researchers would resolve this tension.
